+# Embedding batches and versioning
+
+The indexer sends at most 64 chunks per embedding request and caps one indexing
+operation at 10,000 chunks by default. It rejects missing, non-finite, and
+wrong-dimension vectors before persistence. Every stored vector includes its
+tenant, repository, chunk, provider model, explicit model version, and observed
+dimension so a model migration can build a parallel index instead of silently
+mixing incompatible vectors.

explanations.title: Bounded embedding requests
explanations.summary: Indexing now defaults to batches of 64 and rejects operations above 10,000 chunks before calling the provider. Both limits can be overridden.

explanations.title: Batches can persist incrementally
explanations.summary: Batches are stored as they complete, so an error in a later batch can leave earlier batches persisted.

explanations.title: Validate embedding inputs and responses
explanations.summary: The indexer rejects chunks without an ID or content, and fails if the provider returns a different number of vectors than inputs. It checks vectors before storing them.

explanations.title: Persist embedding provenance
explanations.summary: Each stored embedding is associated with its installation, repository, chunk, model, explicit model version, and observed dimension, allowing versions to be tracked separately.

explanations.title: Reject invalid vectors
explanations.summary: Vectors must be non-empty, finite, and match the configured dimension when one is set; invalid vectors are rejected before persistence.

explanations.title: Track versions for existing and new embeddings
explanations.summary: Existing chunks receive the non-null value `legacy`; removing the default means future inserts must provide an embedding model version explicitly.
